title: Dependency graph + version gatekeeper for upgrade preflight
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Ship a reusable Dependency Graph generator and a Version Gatekeeper service that run as part of release preflight. The tool will construct a directed graph of components (runtime, model-packages, kernel-binaries, deploy-time adapters, console routes) and assert compatibility constraints against target channels (stable, LTS, nightly).

Why: Current preflight checks are stateless smoke/eval runs that miss cross-component version incompatibilities (eg. runtime > kernel ABI mismatch, model tokenizer schema changes that require adapter bump). A graph-first gate lets us detect structural incompatibilities early and run targeted smoke + perf suites only where risk is high.

Deliverables:
- dependency-graph generator (python tool) that crawls manifests (deployment manifests, model-metadata, kernel-catalog) and outputs node/edge list + version ranges. Output format: newline-delimited JSON records (one flat JSON object per line) for downstream pipeline.
- version-gatekeeper microservice (k8s job + lightweight REST) that:
  * ingests graph and release target (e.g., runtime:1.22, lts-channel:2025-Q4)
  * computes a minimal set of impacted components and failure modes (ABI, schema, protocol)
  * emits gating directives: run-smoke-battery for nodes X,Y; warmup-KV-cache for request-pattern Z; mark model-variant fallback mapping if mismatch found
- integration with release-runner so gates veto or tag rollout (auto-fail if high-risk incompatibility)
- runbook + Confluence page describing how to interpret gate outputs and remediation steps

Acceptance criteria:
1) Graph generator runs against a canary infra snapshot and produces node list with < 2% missing references vs manual inventory.
2) Gatekeeper flags at least 3 demonstrated incompatibility scenarios (simulated kernel ABI mismatch, tokenizer-version drift, and quantization metadata schema change) and provides actionable directives.
3) Gate outputs are surfaced as structured comments in the release PR and as signals to the console rollout UI (via /api/internal/release-gates).
4) Automated test harness runs the targeted smoke battery indicated by the gate and returns pass/fail within SLA (30m) for dedicated-capacity regressions.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Semver vs explicit compatibility matrix: we will default to semver ranges where available, but maintain an override compatibility matrix for kernel-binaries and tokenizer schema because those are not strictly semver-managed today. This minimizes false positives while ensuring correctness for sensitive subsystems.
- Graph freshness: generator will be scheduled as a periodic job (every 6 hours) and run on-demand during release creation. We accept ~10 minute cold-start for on-demand runs.
- Granularity of smoke selection: Gatekeeper selects smoke suites by risk score (component criticality * delta-size). Risk score threshold configurable per release tier (stable/LTS have lower thresholds).
- Performance gating heuristics: Use 95th percentile token latency and rolling-median of throughput to spot regressions. Absolute thresholds for LTS will be stricter (eg. latency +10ms, throughput -5% from baseline).

Integration and artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Dependency+Graph+and+Gatekeeper+Spec
- Design diagram (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b-gatekeeper-arch
- Initial GitHub prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dep-graph-gatekeeper (WIP)
- Draft runbook PR for release-runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-runner/pull/412

Operational considerations:
- Gatekeeper will emit structured JSON results with severity tags: INFO | WARNING | BLOCKER. Release-runner will treat BLOCKER as automatic block, WARNING as signal requiring human approval.
- Audit logs stored in the release artifact bucket for 90 days; keep summary in console for 30 days.
- Security: tool only needs read access to manifests and write access to release metadata; no secrets required. We will request a short security review focused on least-privilege RBAC for the k8s job.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Spike: wire up generator to runtime manifests and produce a canonical graph (owner: Ravi) — due 2026-02-22
- Prototype gate decision rules (owner: Ava) — due 2026-02-28
- Hook gate outputs to the smoke-runner job and run three simulated incompatibility scenarios on staging (owner: release-engineering) — due 2026-03-10
- Deliver runbook and merge integration PRs (owners: platform and release teams) — due 2026-03-20

Notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on the decisioning layer and integration surface. Separate follow-ups will generalize the graph schema and add a UI visualization in the console that lets release engineers explore the graph and interactively re-run targeted suites.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ravi: Spike started. Pulled runtime and kernel manifests; discovered inconsistent kernel 'abi' field across 2 manifests. Added temporary mapping rule to generator to normalize older key names.
2026-02-18 - Ava: Reviewed prototype output. Found duplicate nodes for 'tokenizer-service' due to differing model-metadata locations. Decided to canonicalize by service id + sha256(manifest_path).
2026-02-22 - Ravi: Spike complete. Canonical graph produced for canary snapshot. Missing references < 1.2% (mostly deprecated adapters). Uploaded sample output to Drive and linked above.
2026-02-25 - Kofi Mensah (release lead): Requested stricter blocking semantics for LTS channels. We will treat ABI mismatches as BLOCKER by default for lts-2025-Q4.
2026-03-02 - Design review: Sarah (platform design) suggested adding a lightweight tree visualization in the PR comment to aid owners; moving visualization to a follow-up to keep scope small.

2026-03-08 - QA: Ran 3 simulated failure scenarios. Gatekeeper flagged tokenizer schema drift and recommended model-variant fallback; smoke-runner detected latency regression in kernel path and returned WARNING. One blocker scenario (ABI mismatch) caused auto-block as expected.

2026-03-10 - Ravi: Prepared PR #58 in dep-graph-gatekeeper with basic ingestion and decision rules. Opening integration PRs to release-runner next.
